- When sentiment is positive (≥0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.00) or neutral, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak.
- If 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend in history, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; add 1–2% upward bias to counteract.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to be too optimistic in early days (first 5–7) when sentiment is weak; dampen initial forecast values.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model may be overly conservative; increase forecast by 2–3% to reflect latent market momentum.
- When sentiment spikes to 0.67 or above, model often fails to capture volatility; add 1–2% volatility buffer to forecast range.
